title: Canonical continuous-function realization for totally disconnected normed fields
statement: For a normed field E with totally disconnected topology and any scheme X, the condensed coefficient ring of continuous E-valued functions is canonically isomorphic as a ring sheaf to the continuous-function ring sheaf on X_proet. The isomorphism is uniquely characterized by the adjoint equations on every profinite test function. In particular this applies to finite normed p-adic extensions on topologically noetherian X. The chosen isomorphism is determined uniquely, not chosen from undetermined existence.

Prove naturality using the prime-spectrum homeomorphism for locally constant integer-valued functions and pullback projection identities. Transpose through the existing monoidal adjunction; the pushforward ring-object identity proves multiplicativity.

Its explicit locally constant integer spectrum lift, affine transport, relative pullback-map equivalence and connected-components factorization identify maps U → X[S] with continuous maps π₀(U) → S for every affine U, with the evaluation formula needed below. No witness is chosen from the public existence theorem.

proof.text: Naturality of the profinite projection shows target naturality of this normalized equivalence. Its inverse applied to the identity defines the canonical component arrow q:U → X[π₀(U)]. The equivalence and its target naturality show q is terminal in the opposite comma category. For a pointwise left Kan extension the corresponding cocone leg a is invertible by IsColimit.isIso_ι_app_of_isTerminal. Naturality of the comparison σ and its adjoint equation identify a followed by σ(U) with pullback of continuous functions along q. The normalization identifies this with composition along U → π₀(U). Surjectivity of the component quotient gives injectivity, and Continuous.connectedComponentsLift gives surjectivity for a totally disconnected coefficient field. Thus σ(U) is invertible.

proof.text: On weakly contractible affine objects use lem-weil-pbc-proetale-sheafification-wcontractible-sections to identify the sheafification unit as invertible. Uniqueness of left adjoints compares this sheafified Kan construction with the given composite inverse image. The affine covers in lem-weil-pbc-proetale-affine-wcontractible-covering-family detect local bijectivity, hence the resulting ring-sheaf comparison is invertible. The adjoint equations on all test functions determine uniqueness. A finite normed p-adic extension is totally disconnected via its finite-dimensional coordinate homeomorphism, so the final specialization follows from the general theorem.
